A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Programming by Backprop (PBB), with identifiable continuity in curricula, datasets, and experiments despite substantial revision. Both complete documents, including their appendices, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on Random Arithmetic, Leetcode, and custom ciphers, including composition, data-scaling, and training-algorithm analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports original PBB experiments, including Qwen3 evaluations, grammar generation, sample-efficiency comparisons, and additional controls, alongside earlier analyses.

M1.justification: The core proactive and retroactive two-stage curricula persist. v2 adds a cipher variant combining instruction modelling with skewed execution demonstrations during stage 2 (Section 5.2, Figure 5), whereas v1 compares code training and demonstration training separately. The broader formal description and grammar application do not establish a new core algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds sentence generation under 200 synthetic context-free grammars with five vocabularies (Section 4.1), extending evaluation beyond algorithm execution to grammatical compliance. Random Arithmetic, Leetcode, and custom-cipher coverage remain.

E2.justification: v2 adds an algorithm-distillation comparison on Random Arithmetic with the same first-stage training, explicit in-context execution comparisons, a random-generation grammar baseline, and the combined instruction-plus-demonstration cipher condition (Figures 2, 3, 5, and 6). The earlier SFT, DPO, and GRPO comparisons remain.

E3.justification: v2 makes Qwen3 4B/8B/14B the primary models while retaining Llama evaluations. Stated settings change from one SFT epoch to five, from 90 Random Arithmetic SFT execution examples per training function to 30, and from GRPO group/batch sizes 6/6 to 8/32; learning rates and schedules also change. Grammar parsing and the demonstration-count sweep introduce additional protocols. These reported revisions do not establish that every retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds Random Arithmetic stage-isolation controls, execution-only retroactive training controls (Appendix H), instruction-versus-demonstration efficiency curves, and an analysis of combining instructions with biased cipher demonstrations. Representation analyses also cover more models. Earlier data-scaling, single-stage versus two-stage, and DPO/GRPO analyses remain in Appendices B-D.

E5.justification: Both versions report evaluation over 16 samples with 95% confidence intervals. v2 removes v1's explicit disclosure that training uses a single seed. It does not document an increase in independent training runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive Qwen3 and grammar results, including reported 37% average Random Arithmetic execution accuracy for Qwen3-14B, approximately 47% proactive grammar compliance versus approximately 6% random compliance, and the comparison with up to 100 demonstrations. Figure 5 newly shows the hybrid cipher condition outperforming both individual training sources. Several older appendix plots remain unchanged; new scores under changed settings are not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Section 3 introduces explicit instruction denotations covering both functions and grammar-generated languages, context pointers, and specialization mappings. The accompanying loss and gradient expressions largely formalize the existing curricula. This is a limited extension of the mathematical definitions, without new theorems, proofs, or guarantees.

C1.justification: v1 centers PBB as a possible explanation for reasoning benefits from code training. v2 presents it as a general regime for acquiring behavior from declarative instructions across code and grammars. Its title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion make curriculum design and the new claim that one instruction can substitute for up to 100 demonstrations central contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning delayed SFT generalization, reduced retroactive benefits in familiar domains, and grammar compliance as implicit syntactic computation. It qualifies sample efficiency by the amortized first-stage cost and discusses natural-language PBB as a scaling and representation problem (Appendix F.1). Conversely, v1's explicit limitations concerning synthetic tasks and extrapolation from finetuning to pretraining are omitted.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code/data repository link and release statement, grammar-generation and parser details, explicit RL reward and KL settings, and clarification of the scaling experiment's fixed unpaired set. It removes v1's Adam parameters, gradient-clipping detail, precise cipher definitions, and several I/O split specifications. The MathInstruct mixture is no longer documented. These are substantial changes to reproducibility information, including both additions and losses.

R1.justification: Research positioning is substantially rewritten around learning to execute, declarative knowledge, and curriculum design. Added connections include neural interpreters and execution engines, classical partial evaluation, latent learning, and continual pretraining. Several earlier references and contrasts disappear, including the discussion of Thomm et al.'s composition limits. v2 also more explicitly identifies proactive PBB with the earlier implicit-meta-learning pipeline.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, method exposition, and results narrative are extensively rewritten. Results are reorganized around algorithmic execution, sample efficiency, and grammar compliance. The discussion-and-limitations section is replaced by a conclusion and reproducibility statement, with new natural-language discussion in Appendix F.1.

P2.justification: v2 redraws Figure 1, introduces a six-panel main comparison, adds sample-efficiency and grammar figures, expands the cipher plot, and moves Llama results to Appendix A. Several earlier appendix plots are retained and renumbered. Conference formatting changes the layout throughout. The new Figure 3 caption incorrectly interchanges the descriptions of its upper-right and lower-right panels.

improvement.justification: The matched-first-stage demonstration comparison, additional stage-isolation controls, and non-code grammar experiments substantially strengthen the empirical case for PBB's efficiency and applicability beyond code. They address questions that v1's code-centered evidence left unresolved. The repository information also improves access documentation. Lost seed, implementation, and limitation disclosures, together with figure-labeling errors, reduce transparency and clarity, but the stronger experimental support provides a substantial net improvement.
